speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the impact of the SolarWinds breach on Singapore and the cybersecurity of our critical systems; and (b) what steps is the Ministry taking to mitigate the cyber threats to Singapore arising from this and other global cybersecurity incidents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in light of the SolarWinds cybersecurity incident (a) how many companies and Government agencies are affected or vulnerable to such attacks; and (b) how can companies providing essential services and Government agencies have better oversight over cybersecurity arrangements with third party providers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The attacker used the software’s regular updates to implant a backdoor and gain a foothold in the networks of organisations that downloaded and installed the malicious update.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is a very sophisticated attack that evaded detection for many months.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This breach is especially noteworthy because the SolarWinds software is part of the network control and management infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Hence, it was trusted and had privileged access to internal networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The situation is still evolving and the affected firms are continuing with their investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Government is nonetheless adopting a cautious approach and CSA has issued public advisories on steps that enterprises and organisations should take to safeguard their systems against this threat.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: These include having full visibility of their networks and detecting unusual activity in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: At its core, this "zero-trust" cybersecurity posture has the notion that we should protect our networks by observing two key principles.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: First, we should not trust any activity without first verifying it; and second, ensure constant monitoring and vigilance for suspicious activities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This includes compartmentalising and restricting access to different segments of the network, validating transactions across segments, reconciling any escalation of user privileges, and actively and regularly hunting for threats.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Organisations should also put in place robust plans for cyber incident response in the event they fall victim to a cyber-attack.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: CSA will strengthen engagements with CII sectors, enterprises and organisations to adopt and sustain these measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Given the nature of the digital domain, such cyber incidents will happen from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Malicious actors only need to exploit one vulnerability, while the defenders must ensure that there are no vulnerabilities in all the systems and networks that they are protecting, all the time.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Though difficult to completely prevent, we need deliberate, targeted and consistent efforts to strengthen our cyber defences against sophisticated threats like the SolarWinds breach, which exploit the supply chain of trusted software and vendors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our CIIs, enterprises and citizens must also maintain their vigilance against cyber threats, as we mitigate the risks while leveraging the opportunities of digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I have two points of clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first, is before the SolarWinds incident, FireEye was also a victim of hacks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: According to media reports, 30% of companies have actually not used SolarWinds nor FireEye software.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This means that the vulnerability could be a lot more extensive than we believe.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How would the Government go ahead in the future to make sure that we close up our weakest link?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second point of clarification is on the roles of CSA and GovTech, in helping our companies providing essential services to toughen up their defences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Not all companies are equally well-resourced, some will need more support than others, we are probably only as good as our weakest link.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, I hope the Minister can point us the way forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think his two questions are in some ways inter-related.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, always be vigilant, constantly evaluate our systems and conduct regular monitoring and threat hunting exercises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think this is a fundamental; it is a posture that we need to adopt across not just our critical information infrastructure, but indeed across all organisations, especially as our digital footprint grows as we adopt new digital solutions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is an important part of our work going forward, raising awareness of cybersecurity and also putting in place solutions or making available solutions which businesses can use, and at the same time also working with individuals.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, there is a range of measures we are undertaking and that we continue to undertake.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think the fact of the matter is, we can never be foolproof in this effort, but we can make sure that we take every effort to strengthen our system and learn from incidents like SolarWinds to further fortify ourselves.
